input.summary:
Roofs part fixed: the A and C mansard roofs now keep the attic-ladder cells (x=4 and x=26, z=23, y18..20) that the stairs part owns, so the roof no longer writes over them.
The roofs line in ./make.sh shows no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE; make.sh wrote build.nbt with all 18 parts.
Only parts/roofs.mjs was edited (two keep boxes added, one per mansard).

waste.what: Working out which cells collided: I read the refusal line, then edited the keep lists by hand from the plan's ladder coordinates instead of reading stairs.mjs or asking the tool which cells the roof would take from earlier parts.
waste.cost: 2 extra tool rounds plus 2 full make.sh runs to confirm; about 4 cells traced by hand
waste.tool: runParts refusal report could name the earlier part that owns each refused cell (here: 'ladder, placed by stairs') and print a ready-made keep box; a preflight such as `mcd roof --keep-owned` would drop those cells from the roof spec automatically.

waste.what: Checking the keep box form: I read the roof tool's commit/keep code to confirm that keep boxes are never written before trusting the fix.
waste.tool: A note in the roof spec docs or the --spec help saying keep boxes are hard-skipped at commit would have saved the grep.

companions.task: Look at the back mansard slope at x=4 and x=26, z=23, y18..20: the two ladder cells are now left open in the eave, so decide whether the roof should close them (a slate cover or trapdoor hatch) or whether the open cells read as a deliberate attic hatch.

left: Attic ladder cells at (4,18..20,23) and (26,18..20,23) are kept free of roof, so the back eave of A and C has an open notch there; not yet checked with mcd check or render, and the slater should decide whether to close it.
Roof part still has no roof.json, so the roof tool skips that step (existing behaviour, not caused by this fix).
